$comment: Canonical screen/navigation map. Built from iOS's Support/AppRoute.swift + ContentView.swift, Android's ui/ProsaryApp.kt NavHost, and Windows's Navigation/Router.cs usage across Views/*.xaml.cs. Parameter names/types here are the logical contract every platform's own route/query-param/navigation-parameter mechanism should carry, not literal syntax. Keep in sync whenever a screen or its parameters change on any platform — see README.md in this directory.

home.purpose: Three devotion cards (Rosary/Angelus/Jesus Prayer) showing each kind's default favorite, plus My Favorites/Settings/About.

favorites.purpose: List of saved favorites grouped by kind, with Pray/Edit/Delete/Set-Default actions and an Add-new button per kind.

favoriteEditor.purpose: Create or edit a favorite of any kind; kind-specific sections shown conditionally.

prayerId.description: Editing an existing favorite. Null when creating new.

newFavoriteKind.description: Seeds a brand-new favorite's kind when prayerId is null. iOS passes the whole ad-hoc Prayer object directly instead (sheet(item:)); Android/Windows thread this + prayerId as separate params since neither has an iOS-sheet-style whole-object-across-navigation mechanism.

rosaryFlow.purpose: The Rosary prayer flow — season bar, progress, bead track, mystery image/text, Back/Next footer.

prayerId.description: Favorite to pray; null falls back to the default Rosary favorite.

reachedVia.iOS: The generic prayer(id) route -> PrayerDispatchView resolves the Prayer and picks the flow by kind.
reachedVia.android: The generic prayer/{id} route -> PrayerDispatchScreen, same dispatch-by-kind pattern.
reachedVia.windows: Routed to directly by name (RosaryPrayerPage) — Home/Favorites already hold the full Prayer in memory, so Windows skips the generic-dispatcher indirection entirely (see ARCHITECTURE.md, "Skip iOS's PrayerDispatchView indirection").

angelusFlow.purpose: The Angelus prayer flow — fixed 7-step sequence, or a single Regina Caeli step during Eastertide. No bead track. Has its own favorite-star toggle since it can be launched with no saved favorite at all.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite. Null when launched from Home with no Angelus favorite saved yet — language borrowed from the default Rosary favorite in that case.

stationsFlow.purpose: The Stations of the Cross flow — opening prayer, each of the 14 stations in order (versicle/response + meditation), closing prayer. No bead track (unlike Rosary/Franciscan Crown/Seven Sorrows/Divine Mercy) — a plain 'N of 16' progress bar, same chrome as angelusFlow/jesusPrayerFlow.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite. Null when launched from Home with no Stations favorite saved yet — same pattern as angelusFlow, but Stations has no fallback-language favorite to borrow from since it has no kind-specific options at all; falls back to the app's default language directly.

franciscanCrownFlow.purpose: The Franciscan Crown flow — Sign of the Cross, 7 decades of the Seven Joys of Mary (Our Father + 10 Hail Marys each, bead-tracked like the Rosary), 2 closing Hail Marys + 1 closing Our Father, the seasonal Marian antiphon, closing Sign of the Cross. Has a bead track (unlike stationsFlow) despite having no user-configurable options (unlike rosaryFlow) — see mysteries.json's franciscanCrownSevenJoys for the Seven Joys catalog.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite. Null when launched from Home with no Franciscan Crown favorite saved yet — same no-options pattern as angelusFlow/stationsFlow, falls back to the app's default language.

sources.note: Windows duplicates RosaryPrayerPage's full bead-track XAML/ViewModel logic here rather than sharing it (that platform has no PrayerStepFlowControl-style abstraction for the bead track) — see FranciscanCrownViewModel.cs's own doc comment.

sevenSorrowsFlow.purpose: The Seven Sorrows (Servite Rosary/Chaplet of Our Lady of Sorrows) flow — Sign of the Cross, 7 decades of the Seven Sorrows of Mary (Our Father + 7 Hail Marys each, bead-tracked like the Rosary/Franciscan Crown), 3 closing Hail Marys for Our Lady's tears, a fixed closing versicle/response/collect, closing Sign of the Cross. Has a bead track (unlike stationsFlow) despite having no user-configurable options (unlike rosaryFlow), same as franciscanCrownFlow — see seven-sorrows.json for the catalog. Unlike franciscanCrownFlow, the closing prayer is fixed (not the Rosary's Marian-antiphon picker) and every decade uses 7 Hail Marys, not 10 (see ARCHITECTURE.md's Bead progress track section for the beads-per-decade generalization this required).

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite. Null when launched from Home with no Seven Sorrows favorite saved yet — same no-options pattern as angelusFlow/stationsFlow/franciscanCrownFlow, falls back to the app's default language.

sources.note: Windows duplicates RosaryPrayerPage's full bead-track XAML/ViewModel logic here too, same reasoning as franciscanCrownFlow's note — this is now the 3rd near-identical copy (Rosary/Franciscan Crown/Seven Sorrows), flagged in SevenSorrowsViewModel.cs's doc comment as a strong candidate for extraction into a shared control.

divineMercyFlow.purpose: The Divine Mercy Chaplet flow — Sign of the Cross, Our Father, Hail Mary, the Apostles' Creed (opening, reusing existing prayer content), 5 decades each of one offering + 10 petitions (the same two lines repeated every decade, unlike rosaryFlow/franciscanCrownFlow/sevenSorrowsFlow), the closing acclamation prayed 3 times, closing Sign of the Cross. Has a bead track (unlike stationsFlow) despite having no user-configurable options (unlike rosaryFlow), same as franciscanCrownFlow/sevenSorrowsFlow. The lightest of the four rollout devotions: no per-decade catalog at all — every step reuses one image (divine_mercy_image), the same reuse pattern angelusFlow uses for joyful_01_annunciation.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite. Null when launched from Home with no Divine Mercy Chaplet favorite saved yet — same no-options pattern as angelusFlow/stationsFlow/franciscanCrownFlow/sevenSorrowsFlow, falls back to the app's default language.

sources.note: Windows duplicates RosaryPrayerPage's full bead-track XAML/ViewModel logic here too — this is now the 4th near-identical copy (Rosary/Franciscan Crown/Seven Sorrows/Divine Mercy Chaplet), flagged in DivineMercyViewModel.cs's doc comment as a strong candidate for extraction into a shared control.

jesusPrayerSetup.purpose: Repetition-count picker (33/66/99/Custom/Unbounded) before starting a fresh Jesus Prayer session.

jesusPrayerFlow.purpose: The Jesus Prayer flow — single fixed line + repetition counter, no engine. Own favorite-star toggle, same reason as angelusFlow.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite — its own target overrides target, and its language is used.

target.description: Set when launched fresh from jesusPrayerSetup (no favorite yet).

jesusPrayerFlow.navigationNote: Finish (pop-to-Home) and the back arrow (pop-one-level, back to Setup) are deliberately distinct commands — see ARCHITECTURE.md and JesusPrayerViewModel's class doc.

about.purpose: Attribution: typefaces, mystery/other image sources, Scripture sources. Static content.

sources.iOS: Views/About/AboutView.swift (Mac: app-menu-only, own window; iPhone/iPad: linked from Home)

settings.purpose: App-wide preferences — currently just the default prayer language.

sources.iOS: Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift (macOS Settings scene, Cmd+,; iOS has no in-app equivalent — the system Settings app via Settings.bundle/Root.plist instead)
sources.android: ui/settings/SettingsScreen.kt (Android has no external settings surface to extend, unlike iOS)
